source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment, Ch. 6 (Soils).

sections.heading: 1. Soil — Basics and Classification
points: **Soil** = the uppermost weathered layer of the earth's crust, a mixture of mineral particles and organic matter (humus) supporting plant life.
The **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)** classifies Indian soils into 8 major types.
Soil formation depends on parent rock, climate, relief, vegetation and time.

sections.heading: 2. Major Soil Types
points: **Alluvial soil** — most widespread and fertile (northern plains, deltas, coasts); rich in potash; **Khadar (new)** and **Bhangar (old)**; ideal for cereals, sugarcane.
**Black (regur) soil** — from Deccan lava; **moisture-retentive**, rich in iron/lime/magnesia, poor in nitrogen; best for **cotton** (Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat).
**Red and Yellow soil** — on crystalline igneous rocks (Deccan, eastern/southern); reddish (iron), less fertile, need fertilisers.
**Laterite soil** — high rain + high temperature (leaching); acidic, poor in nutrients; good for **tea, coffee, cashew** (Western Ghats, NE).
**Arid (desert) soil** — sandy, saline, low humus (Rajasthan); **Saline (alkaline)** soils; **Peaty/marshy** (high organic, waterlogged); **Forest/mountain** soils.

sections.heading: 3. Soil Erosion and Conservation
points: **Soil erosion** — removal of topsoil by water (sheet, gully → ravines/badlands like Chambal) and wind; worsened by deforestation, overgrazing, faulty farming.

sub: **Contour ploughing, terracing, strip cropping** (against water erosion on slopes).
**Afforestation, controlled grazing, crop rotation** and check dams/gully plugging.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Alluvial = most widespread and fertile (Khadar new, Bhangar old).
Laterite = leaching (high rain), good for tea/coffee/cashew.
Arid soil = sandy/saline (Rajasthan); Chambal = ravines/badlands (gully erosion).
Conservation: contour ploughing, terracing, shelter belts, afforestation.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Black (regur) soil is best for cotton** and formed from **lava**.
**Alluvial soil is the most widespread and fertile** in India.
**Laterite soil forms by leaching** in high-rainfall areas (poor in nutrients).
The **Chambal ravines** are formed by **gully erosion** (badlands).
